effort: Close space, brake in time and deny the opponent’s first exit.
brief: Use the retreat/recovery context to train the opposite problem: approaching without overrunning. E1 is a controlled closeout with a live exit. Vertical extension/landing, forward obstacle clearance, a fore–aft single-leg rebound, moving lateral force release and time-to-arrival reading support the brake and next push.
anchor_protocol: In a verified up-to-10 m × 7 m bay, athlete begins at 1 m and approaches a junction at 4 m under control. Coach outside the route and visible beyond it commits left/right before the athlete reaches 3 m. Athlete lowers through the last approach steps, redirects 1 m toward that exit and stops within the next 2 m. Four trials, two each direction. No hand block, collision, extra sprint or airborne attempt to deny the coach. If the plant is uncertain, cue at the start and shorten the approach to 2 m.
quality_marker: E1: select the right exit while keeping the stopping route available, without a reaching final plant or running past the junction. Log approach length, early-cue regression and correct/control results separately.
layout: The junction, two short exits and all buffers must fit within the measured combined bay; coach occupies a protected position outside them, ≥2 m away. E3 uses a low hurdle with clearance verified for the athlete; E4 needs only small forward/back distances. E5 releases a light ball into an empty 2–7 m length of one lane, no return catch. E6 coach rolls a ball on a separate parallel lane while athlete travels on their own marked 2 m route with 2 m stopping space; no attempt to touch/stop the ball and no shared finish corridor. Full-route width is a requirement, not confirmed inventory: branch stopping extensions can exceed a 4 m bay. Compact same-drill option: rotate the E1 T so the approach crosses the width for only 1 m and its 1 m left/right exits plus 2 m stops run along the 10 m lane length. Place the coach ahead of the junction on a separate protected position. Keep four trials, early cue and controlled speed; E1 movement becomes 8 m plus up to 8 m stopping. Verify the approach, body margins and coach space within a 4 m-wide bay. This remains closeout-and-denial, not a new exercise. At setup, mark complete body/landing envelopes, both possible routes, run-off and the coach position; a floor-line diagram alone does not establish clearance. If even the compact footprint is unavailable, resolve the layout before delivery.
progression: Previous: Class 5 prescribed retreat and reopening, with thirteen bilateral landing events. Current: short closeout and eleven jump/rebound landings with four unilateral contacts; no increased entry speed or deception is presumed. Retain squat, hinge and ankle anchors at demonstrated loads; use one working step-up set/leg to avoid turning closeout work into a high-volume eccentric leg day. Progress cue lateness only after actual braking and next-step control, adequate RIR and recovery are reported.
audit: Approach distance and cue location are explicit so late braking is not forced into the last metre. CMJ is first used here, as physical support rather than a generic height test. Forward/back single-leg returns are limited to one pair per leg. Rolling-ball arrival is a timing problem on separate paths, different from Class 3’s release-direction alignment. Next class introduces pass-lane inference with controlled entry. Geometry revision: removed the implication that every full-length angled route fits a 4 m-wide rectangle; added a quantified shorter same-drill alternative. Default ledger totals remain the full-route prescription; compact actual travel is logged separately.

explosive.name: Closeout-to-Exit Denial
explosive.job: Main task: absorb an approach while reading where the opponent can leave, then direct the next step.
explosive.execution: Approach 3 m, take the indicated 1 m exit, stop in 2 m. Coach commits before the final metre of approach. Rest 75 s between trials and 90 s before E2. Cue earlier/shorten approach for overshoot.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Countermovement Jump to Stick
explosive.job: Rapid extension followed by bilateral force acceptance, supporting a tall-to-low closeout transition.
explosive.execution: Natural arm swing, jump vertically and land on both feet; hold 2 s. Do not chase maximal height. Rest 30 s between jumps, 60 s before E3. Lower height for noisy/asymmetric or unstable landings.

explosive.name: Low-Hurdle Forward Jump to Stick
explosive.job: Coordinate forward clearance with deliberate shared-foot braking beyond an external obstacle.
explosive.execution: Two-foot takeoff over one low hurdle, two-foot landing and 2 s hold; walk around to reset, not back-jump. Rest 45 s between attempts, 60 s before E4. Lower hurdle or shorten travel if clearance/landing fails.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Single-Leg Forward–Back Rebound
explosive.job: Reverse a small forward impulse back through the same plant, supporting a closeout that must give ground.
explosive.execution: On one leg hop a short distance forward then immediately back once, stick the return; repeat on the other leg after 75 s. Rest 60 s before E5. Reduce distance for a long or unstable reversal contact.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Step-In Lateral Medicine-Ball Scoop Toss
explosive.job: Convert one incoming step into lateral leg/hip impulse; differs from stationary lateral release by accepting approach momentum.
explosive.execution: Take one deliberate side step, load that hip, pivot both feet as needed and release a light ball sideways into the cleared lane. No jump/catch. Rest 30 s between throws and 60 s before E6. Shorten step/load if the knee twists or the release is slow.

explosive.name: Rolling-Ball Arrival Intercept
explosive.job: Judge time to arrival, choosing when to leave so the body reaches a line under control before a slow moving object does.
explosive.execution: Coach rolls a light ball 3 m along the separate path at a moderate consistent speed. Athlete may choose the departure moment, travel 2 m to their own parallel line and stop within 2 m. No ball contact. Rest 60 s between trials and 90 s before strength. Slow the roll if the only solution is an unsafe rush.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

stabilization.name: Lateral Step-Down — light dumbbell
stabilization.job: Easy knee/pelvis alignment in controlled lowering before the closeout-related strength work.
stabilization.execution: Lower for 3 s from a suitably low stable platform, free heel lightly taps; keep standing heel down. Use bodyweight or reduce range for pelvic/knee drift. If no platform fits, use a shallow supported single-leg squat instead, same dose. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

stabilization.name: Short-Foot Drill — both feet supported
stabilization.job: Preserve the planted tripod during the transition from braking to pushing.
stabilization.execution: Keep both feet supported and work one target foot at a time: maintain heel and metatarsal contact while gently raising the arch, with long toes. Relax 5 s between holds; use seated support instead if toes curl. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

primary.name: Goblet Squat
primary.job: Load whole-leg force acceptance and return from the lowered closeout stance.
primary.execution: Hold one dumbbell at the chest; sit between the hips with whole-foot pressure and rise smoothly. Use an owned depth; reduce load/range for heel lift or trunk collapse. 120 s between rounds and 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
primary.job: Lead-leg extension and a controlled descent without extra lateral lunge volume.
primary.execution: Use a stable box below the point where the pelvis tilts; whole lead foot supported. Drive up without a trailing-leg hop and step down under control. Lower box/load if the return drops. If no box fits, use floor-supported Split Squat instead at the same sets/reps per leg, 2–3 RIR, with no other split-squat slot in this class. Rest 90 s between sides; 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
primary.job: Hip hinge contributes to decelerating the approach without collapsing the trunk.
primary.execution: Hinge from standing with soft knees; keep weights close and stop descent where the pelvis/spine remain controlled. Finish tall without leaning back. Reduce range/load for rounding. Rest 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Copenhagen Plank — Short Lever
primary.job: Adductor/pelvis support during the immediate lateral denial step.
primary.execution: Upper knee bent about 90 degrees on a stable bench, forearm under shoulder; lift the lower leg and keep pelvis level. Select a short lever with about 5 seconds clean hold reserve. Stop for groin, shoulder or knee pain. If bench/support is unsuitable, use side-lying hip adduction instead, 1 × 8/side at 2–3 RIR; record changed hold/repetition totals. For that replacement, prepare with 1 × 4 easy reps/side instead of the two 5 s preparation holds; retain side rest. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 s/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise — supported standing, dumbbell
primary.job: Straight-knee push during the approach-to-exit transition.
primary.execution: Stand on flat floor with a nearly straight knee and light hand support; raise the heel, pause briefly and lower for 2 seconds. No bounce or ankle roll. Reduce load when heel height declines. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, bent-knee
primary.job: Bent-knee ankle force in the closeout brake and low first exit step.
primary.execution: Use a stable bench, knees near right angles, secure dumbbells on distal thighs above knees. Lower heels for 2 seconds to the floor, pause, then rise. Reduce load for bouncing or shortened range. Rest 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.
